description:
Give `jit graph export` a scoped, batch-shaped output mode so a container's subgraph can be captured in the exact schema `jit issue batch-create --from-json` consumes — a first-class inverse of batch creation.

## Background

Batch creation reads an array of issue definitions with symbolic keys and per-node `depends_on`, pre-validates the whole file, and creates the subgraph in one operation. No export produces that shape: `jit graph export --format json` emits the whole graph as UUID-keyed nodes with a separate edge list, has no subgraph selection, and carries lifecycle fields (state, assignee, timestamps) and identity-bound labels that batch creation neither accepts nor should recreate. Round-tripping a subtree today means hand-written jq over the full export, with silently improvised answers to boundary edges, bracket-infrastructure nodes, and label hygiene.

The membership closure needed for scoping already exists: per-container DAG-authoritative membership is computed by the scoped validation path. The batch schema is fixed by batch creation: `key`, `title`, `description`, `type`, `priority`, `labels`, `gates`, `depends_on` (symbolic keys).

A scoped batch export is also the capture dual of graph templates: `jit apply <template> <container>` instantiates an abstract parameterized subgraph from the registry, while this export captures a concrete subgraph as a replayable seed. Promoting a captured seed into a registered template (parameterizing titles and labels) is a natural follow-up and out of scope here; the linked use-cases document develops the relationship.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `jit graph export --scope <container>` restricts export to the container's DAG-authoritative membership closure and composes with every existing format (json, dot, mermaid).
- [hard] REQ-02: `jit graph export --format batch` emits a JSON array in the batch-create input schema: per node a symbolic `key` (the short id), `title`, `description`, `type` (from the node's type label), `priority`, `labels`, `gates` (the node's gate set), and `depends_on` listing in-scope symbolic keys.
- [hard] REQ-03: Batch output carries no lifecycle fields (state, assignee, timestamps), and every in-scope node exports regardless of its state.
- [hard] REQ-04: Batch output strips identity-bound labels — membership labels per `[type_hierarchy.label_associations]`, the coverage rule's satisfies-namespace labels, and `brackets:*` — while generic labels survive.
- [hard] REQ-05: Nodes whose type matches a template's planning- or breakdown-role node type are excluded from batch output together with their edges.
- [hard] REQ-06: Edges crossing the scope boundary are excluded from batch output and reported in the command's output (count and node pairs); none are dropped silently.
- [hard] REQ-07: Round-trip holds: the batch export of a container's subtree, fed to batch creation in a fresh repository with compatible configuration, recreates an isomorphic subgraph (same titles, types, priorities, gates, and in-scope edges) and passes repository validation; a harness test covers this.
- [hard] REQ-08: `--format batch` without `--scope` exports the whole graph in batch shape; existing formats and flags behave unchanged when the new flags are absent.

## Notes

Decisions pinned during intake:

- **CLI shape: extend `jit graph export`** with orthogonal `--scope` and `--format batch`. Rejected: a dedicated capture subcommand — scoping benefits every existing format (scoped Mermaid and DOT diagrams fall out free), and one export surface stays discoverable.
- **Lifecycle policy: strip all, include all.** The output is a pure structural seed; batch creation always makes fresh backlog issues. Rejected: default state filtering — excluding done nodes punches holes in dependency chains and forces edge contraction; a state filter can be added later if a use case demands it.
- **Boundary and bracket policy: exclude and report.** Boundary-crossing edges are listed, bracket-infrastructure nodes are excluded so the target re-scaffolds its own bracket via the graph template. Rejected: verbatim export — every import would need manual pruning and duplicate bracket nodes.
- **Label policy: strip identity-bound, keep generic.** Membership and satisfies labels reference the source container's identity and criteria ids; recreating them in a target is guaranteed-wrong. Rejected: verbatim labels.
title: Scoped batch-shape graph export as the batch-create inverse
